newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar-linked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar-linked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed moderately higher on Thursday in thin trading with dollar-linked bonds rising more sharply following the decline of the shekel in the local foreign currency market, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years):
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 160.73
Volume was low at 107 million shekels.
"Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply following the decline of the shekel against the dollar," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2560 shekels against 3.2320 on Thursday after newspaper reports, later denied, said the Bank of Israel would cut short-term interest rates sharply after the government had won seven billion shekels in budget cuts from parliament.

"Trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed and trendless. Despite some profit taking, the bonds closed almost unchanged. It appears that inflation-linked bonds have reached a ceiling at current levels," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

Traders noted that unlinked bonds continued to rise despite low yields. "Even though unlinked bonds rose sharply during the last two months, investors belive that in the long run interest rates will continue to decline," Weiss said.
The First International trader said prices of unlinked bonds reflect expectations for an interest rate cut on Monday of 0.2-0.3 percentage points from the current 15.2 percent.
Traders said the Makam was also rising on hopes for a rate cut, but turnover in the Makam was a very low 24 million shekels.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
